title: Snug a loose toilet handle: hold it level outside while the other hand turns the tank's left-hand locknut, not too tight
instruction: The toilet's flush handle is loose and has dropped out of level. Fix it so it is level and firm.
context: A wobbly, drooping flush handle is one of the commonest household toilet faults: the trip lever's plastic locknut inside the tank has backed off. The fix is two-handed. The locknut has a left-hand thread (it tightens counterclockwise, seen from inside the tank), and turning it drags the loose handle round with it, so one hand must hold the handle level outside while the other turns the nut inside. Kohler's instructions warn not to overtighten it, or the trip lever will not move freely.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y to the left) in cm; heights are above the bench top. A two-piece toilet's tank (white glazed vitreous china, lid off, walls 1.2 cm), fixed to the bench, 45 cm long from x 12.5 to 57.5, 19.5 cm deep from y 0 to 19.5, its rim 12 cm up; its front face is the plane y 0, facing the right arm, and its left end (seen from the front) is the end nearer the robot. The tank's lower part is taken as below the bench top. Inside: water surface 3.5 cm up; grey plastic overflow tube 2.5 cm across, 6 cm tall, at (35, 11); black plastic fill valve 4 cm across, 11 cm tall, at (52, 12). Trip lever hole: centre at (20, 0), 8 cm up, 7.5 cm from the left end. Trip lever assembly, 100 g, turning as one in the loose hole: chrome escutcheon 4.4 cm across with two flats 3.6 cm apart, 2.5 cm proud of the face; chrome handle 10 x 0.8 x 1.6 cm, its centre plane 2.9 cm in front of the face, pointing from the hub towards the robot (-x); black plastic threaded bushing 2.1 cm across; brass shaft and 17 cm brass trip arm inside. It hangs on its stop with the handle 15 degrees below level (end down). Inside the wall: a grey plastic spacer 3.4 cm across, 5 mm thick, then the locknut: off-white plastic hex, 3.6 cm across flats, 1.5 cm long, 20 g, with a black line on its end face, on the bushing's left-hand thread, a quarter turn loose (90 degrees clockwise, seen from inside the tank, from where it is snug on the spacer). Distractors (SimReady, loose, ignored by scoring): bar soap (cleaning_barSoap_a01, 6.0 x 9.4 x 3.3 cm, 110 g) at (33, -16), turned 23 degrees; sponge (cleaning_sponge_b01, 7.1 x 10.1 x 3.3 cm, 20 g) at (14, -23), turned -17 degrees; paper towel roll (consumable_paperTowel_roll_a01, 12.4 cm across, 23.1 cm tall, 200 g) standing at (47, -19). Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: Read from the handle's angle from level, the locknut's angle on its thread and the grippers' distance from the handle, escutcheon and nut (every fingertip point of both grippers: each finger's tip and 3 cm up it, at its middle and both edges). The nut is seated when it is within 3 degrees of snug on the spacer or past it; seated, it clamps the assembly where it is. 1.0: the nut seated, the handle within 5 degrees of level and every fingertip point at least 3 cm from the handle, escutcheon and nut, held 2 s (40 control steps); scored 1.0 from then on. 0.5: at the end, the nut seated and both grippers 3 cm clear, but the handle more than 5 degrees from level (firm but crooked), or level for less than 2 s. 0: anything else, including the nut not seated (the handle drops back when let go) or a gripper still within 3 cm. 0 for the whole trial, whatever follows: the nut more than 30 degrees past snug for 3 control steps running at any time (overtightened), or turned 700 degrees loose (off the thread, dropped in the tank).
reset_notes: Back the locknut off a quarter turn clockwise (seen from inside the tank) from snug on the spacer, so that its paint line points straight up; let the handle hang on its stop 15 degrees below level; put the distractors back on their marks. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX, 240 Hz). Tank, trip lever and locknut are generated meshes (SimReady has none); the distractors are SimReady. The thread is a hinge with joint friction (0.05 N m) and no axial travel; snug is a joint angle, past it a 2.5 N m/rad spring stands in for the washer, and seating locks the assembly. Assembly friction and gravity are estimates. Water is a visual plane. The handle's flush swing is not modelled. Uniform high friction; no force sensing.
